title: Weight-adjusted waist index adds little albuminuria prediction beyond its component measurements across NHANES cycles
abstract: Frozen weighted logistic models trained on 5,389 NHANES 2009–2010 adults were tested on 4,935 separately sampled 2015–2016 adults. Adding weight-adjusted waist index reduced clinical-factor Brier score by 0.000302 (95% conditional PSU-bootstrap interval −0.000437 to −0.000169). After waist and weight were included, the difference was −0.000059 (−0.000253 to +0.000120); with quadratic components it reversed to +0.000034. Penalty sensitivity also reversed the component-conditional gain. Thus a small transported clinical-baseline gain does not establish new physiological information or superiority over nonlinear component measurements. This is a complete-case cross-sectional prediction audit, not incident kidney disease prediction or fully independent replication of prior pooled-NHANES associations. Code, hashes, predictions, unfavorable sensitivity results, author checks and clean rerun are supplied.
